deities: Adinath (Rishabhanatha, the first Jain Tirthankara - four-faced idol)

history.dynasty: Mewar (Rana Kumbha, r. 1433-1468; Kumbha-era patronage, 15th century)
history.period: Construction begun 1389 per tradition/inscriptions, consecrated 1439 CE; work continued to 1458 (some sources say 1496)
history.summary: CSV TOWN CORRECTION: the Ranakpur Jain Temple is not in Pali town - it stands at the village of Ranakpur near Sadri (Desuri area), Pali district, Rajasthan, in a remote Aravalli valley about 60 km from Pali town. FLAG - JAIN, not a Hindu temple: it is a Svetambara Jain temple dedicated to Adinath (Rishabhanatha), the first Tirthankara of the present half-cycle, and one of the five holiest Jain pilgrimage sites (with Muchhal Mahavir, Narlai, Nadol and Varkana it forms the Gorwad Panch Tirth). History is well documented: a 1436 CE copper-plate record, temple inscriptions and the Sanskrit text Soma-Saubhagya Kavya record that Dharna Shah (Dharnashah), a Porwal Jain minister/businessman from Ghanerao, commenced construction in 1389 after a divine vision of a celestial vehicle; Rana Kumbha of Mewar granted the land and the town was named Ranakpur in his honour. A pillar inscription states that in 1439 Deepaka (Deepa/Dwepa) the architect built the temple at Dharna's direction; Acharya Soma Sundar Suri (Tapa Gaccha) supervised consecration ceremonies. The Chaumukha (four-faced) main temple has 1,444 intricately carved pillars - no two alike - 24 pillared halls, four subsidiary shrines and domes, two 108-kg bells, and carved nymphs at 45 feet. Managed in the past century by the Anandji Kalyanji Pedhi trust. Tradition field records Jain (Svetambara); keep-or-drop decision needed for a Hindu-temples dataset.

name: Ranakpur Jain Temple
town_description: Ranakpur is a village in the Aravalli ranges of Pali district, Rajasthan, near Sadri, named after Rana Kumbha who granted the land for the temple. The Jain temple complex lies in a remote, forested valley about 60 km from Pali town and 90 km north of Udaipur.
tradition: Jain (Svetambara) - NOT a Hindu temple; keep-or-drop decision needed.

travel.airport: Udaipur (Maharana Pratap Airport, ~90 km) and Jodhpur (~150 km) are the nearest airports.
travel.railway: Falna is the nearest railway station (~35 km); Udaipur and Jodhpur are the closest major railheads.
travel.road: Well connected by road via Sadri; Ranakpur is ~60 km from Pali town and ~90 km north of Udaipur on the Pali-Udaipur route.

visitor_information.opening_hours: Darshan hours for non-Jain visitors are commonly reported as 12:00 PM to 5:00 PM (verify - hours not confirmed in consulted sources). Dress modestly; leather articles may be restricted inside Jain shrines.
